title: Evidence for spin swapping from modulation of transverse resistance in magnetic heterostructures with Rashba interface
authors: Heeman Kim, Shutaro Karube, Juan Borge, Junyeon Kim, Kouta Kondou, YoshiChika Otani
abstract: We investigate the transverse response under the out-of-plane magnetic field for magnetic heterostructures with Cu/Bi2O3 or Ag/Bi2O3 Rashba interfaces. We detect opposite contributions on the transverse resistance by the Cu/Bi2O3 and the Ag/Bi2O3 interfaces, which interestingly coincide well with the opposite signs of the spin/charge interconversion from the two interfaces. We suppose the opposite influences on the transverse resistance feature spin swapping occurrence of the converted spin current. The transverse spin flow emerges due to the spin swapping in both Cu and Ag layer, but the direction of the spin flow is opposed dependent on the spin direction of the converted spin current.
summary: This work investigates evidence for 'spin swapping' in magnetic heterostructures by measuring how transverse resistance changes with an out-of-plane magnetic field. The key finding is that opposite signs of the measured resistance modulation correspond to the opposite spin chirality of the Rashba interfaces, supporting a model where spin current direction swaps within the non-magnetic spacer layer.
main_problem: The study investigates evidence for a physical phenomenon called 'spin swapping' by analyzing how the transverse resistance of magnetic heterostructures changes when subjected to an out-of-plane magnetic field.
main_result: Opposite modulations in the transverse resistance ($\Delta R_{xy}$) observed between two different Rashba interfaces (Cu/Bi2O3 vs Ag/Bi2O3) correlate with opposite spin chiralities, suggesting that spin swapping is responsible for generating a transverse spin current with opposing flow directions.
method: The researchers measured the transverse resistance ($R_{xy}$) as a function of an out-of-plane magnetic field ($\mathbf{H}$), calculating $\Delta R_{xy} = R_{xy}(+\mathbf{H}) - R_{xy}(-\mathbf{H})$ to diagnose the spin transport mechanism.
model_or_system: The experiment uses magnetic heterostructures, specifically Py/Cu(or Ag)/Bi2O3, where the Cu or Ag layers act as Rashba interfaces with opposite spin chiralities. The physics is analyzed through the lens of spin-charge conversion and subsequent spin current dynamics.
key_observables: Transverse resistance modulation ($\Delta R_{xy}$), anomalous Hall angle ($	heta_{AH}^{	ext{add}}$), and their dependence on non-magnetic metal (NM) thickness ($t_{	ext{NM}}$).
important_parameters: Out-of-plane magnetic field ($\mathbf{H}$), Rashba interface chirality, and the thickness of the non-magnetic spacer layer ($t_{	ext{NM}}$).
main_assumptions: The spin swapping effect is hypothesized to occur primarily near the ferromagnetic (FM) layer, and intermixing between FM and NM layers is acknowledged as a potential contributing factor.
figures_summary: Figures 1(b) and 1(c) show $R_{xy}$ vs $\mathbf{H}$ demonstrating opposite modulation signs for the two interfaces. Figure 2 shows $	heta_{AH}$ dependence on $t_{	ext{NM}}$, while Figure 3 displays the interface-added contribution ($	heta_{AH}^{	ext{add}}$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the transverse resistance response using magnetic field sweeps and thickness variations, correlating the observed sign changes in transport measurements with theoretical predictions derived from spin chirality differences.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics/condensed matter magnetism, the clear dependence of macroscopic transport properties ($\Delta R_{xy}$) on microscopic symmetry breaking (Rashba interface chirality) provides a tangible experimental test case for complex quantum mechanical spin-orbit coupling effects.
